Only methods declared in candy-top/src, or inherited from a parent declared there, are listed. A type that extends a class outside that tree, such as \RuntimeException, does not show the methods of that class.

App final class

candy-top's root Model: frame layout, theme, clock, cadence, and the panel roster.

MethodSummary
static start(Config $config, Palette $palette, HostInfo $host, array $panels, ?\Closure $clock = null, ?ColorProfile $profile = null, ?\Closure $themes = null, ?ConfigFile $file = null, bool $writeNew = false, ?ThemeRegistry $catalog = null, ?string $unsupportedOs = null, bool $runningAsRoot = false): self
static systemThemes(?string $customDir = null): \ClosureThe live theme loader: the theme $config names, the TTY theme while tty_mode is on (btop Theme::setTheme), read through ThemeRegistry. Only ever called inside a Cmd.
static themeKey(Config $config): stringWhat decides the palette: tty_mode, color_theme, theme_background. A config change that moves it reloads the theme (applyConfig()).
static profileFor(Config $config): ColorProfileThe colour profile $config implies: tty_mode forces 16 colours, else truecolor picks 24-bit over the 256-colour cube (btop Theme::setTheme / Config truecolor).
static programOptions(Config $config, ?ColorProfile $ambient = null): ProgramOptionsThe Program options bin/candy-top runs with: alt screen, 20 fps and btop's mouse reporting — ?1002h button-event tracking + ?1006h SGR (Term::mouse_on, sugar-core CellMotion) unless disable_mouse. Runtime flips of disable_mouse answer with the matching Cmd (applyConfig()).
static terminalReset(): stringThe bytes that put a terminal back after a crash that skipped the Program's own teardown (an exception out of update()/view()/a Cmd escapes Program::run() with no finally): end any synchronized frame, reset SGR, every mouse mode and bracketed paste off, cursor shown, alt screen left — what programOptions() turned on and a little more, all harmless when already off. Raw mode itself is put back by the Tty's destructor.
static pretendBootTimeForTesting(?float $epoch): voidTest seam: pin the boot instant the clock falls back to (null restores live discovery). The suite drives the off-Linux arm this way — /proc/uptime never fails on a Linux host, so without a seam the boot-time fallback could only be reached by lying about the OS.
static pretendBootProbeForTesting(?\Closure $probe): voidTest seam: run the clock as a host without /proc/uptime would, with $probe standing in for the bounded sysctl child discovery (null restores the real OS rules). The Linux suite cannot reach the off-Linux arms — this simulates the SHAPE of such a host (no proc fast path, a probe answering the boot instant) without execing.
static primeBootTime(): voidPrime the boot instant once, at boot, OUTSIDE the event loop. CI wave 5 (5A): the clock closure used to run this discovery inline, and on macOS that meant a synchronous sysctl child inside the loop's first callback — an unbounded exec (shell_exec waits even after SIGTERM) that starved every 20 fps paint behind it when the spawn stalled on the runner. Discovery now belongs to start(), where a bounded child (queryBootTime()) can cost the frame path nothing; the closure only ever reads the memo.
static systemClock(): \ClosureThe live clock Cmd: wall time plus uptime. /proc/uptime answers on Linux; finding 149 adds the off-Linux fallback — discover the boot instant once and subtract it, so %u/%U stop reading a permanent 0 wherever a dependency-free answer exists (BSD family). Windows has none (kern.boottime is BSD-only, GetTickCount64 would need FFI) and keeps the documented 0 rather than a fabricated number.
init(): \Closure
update(Msg $msg): array
view(): string
surface(): ?SurfaceThe painted frame, null before the first WindowSizeMsg. Exactly $rows rows of exactly $cols cells.
freezesBackdrop(): boolbtop's background_update: off — and always in tty mode — the frame behind an open menu is frozen (btop.cpp:664 pause_output, :759).
overlay(): ?OverlayThe menu on top of the stack, or null when none is open.
withOverlay(Overlay $overlay): selfCopy with $overlay opened on top — btop Menu::show. A terminal smaller than the overlay's minimum gets the size-error box instead (OverlayStack::push()).
overlayContext(): OverlayContextThe context an overlay is updated and painted with, built now.
chromeButtons(): arrayThe App-owned cpu title buttons as btop maps them (0-based [x, y, w, h]): m (menu), p (preset — btop {button_y, x + 17, 1, 8}, sized here to the translated label), - and + (update_ms).
clockReserved(): boolTrue when a visible panel asks for btop's clock reserve (ClockReserve; the cpu panel's battery badge).
subscriptions(): ?Subscriptions
clockText(): stringThe clock string as embedded (before the width budget clip).
panel(string $box): ?Panel
panels(): array
panelFor(string $box): ?PanelThe panel drawing box $box: its own roster entry, or — for any gpuN box — the panel registered as gpu (one panel draws every gpu box, btop's Gpu::draw per shown panel).
roster(): GpuRosterThe detected accelerators — btop Gpu::count / gpu_b_height_offsets / gpu_names — as the largest roster any GpuRosterSource panel reports (none before a GPU sample).
withPalette(Palette $palette): selfCopy with a replaced theme (options-menu theme cycling).
applyConfig(Config $config, bool $dirty = true): arraySwap in $config (options menu, presets; SetOptionMsg from a panel). Layout follows it, and so does the colour profile when truecolor / tty_mode change what profileFor() derives (an explicit start() profile survives any change that does not). When tty_mode, color_theme or theme_background change (themeKey()) the returned Cmd also loads the theme the new config asks for — the TTY theme on a tty_mode flip (btop Theme::setTheme) — off the update path and installs it through a PaletteMsg. A changed update_ms bumps $generation AND returns the re-armed data tick, and boxes the new config shows that the old one hid are sampled at once — so the returned Cmd MUST be dispatched: dropping it would leave only the outdated tick armed and stop every data update.
themeCmd(): \ClosureThe Cmd that loads the theme the current config asks for.
dataTick(): \ClosureThe data-tick Cmd for the current period and generation.
logoAnimating(): boolTrue when the chosen art has more than one frame, i.e. there is something to animate at all.
isLogoArmed(): boolTrue while a tick chain for the current logo pick is armed.
logoOverlayOpen(): boolWhether the topmost overlay is one of the three menus that paint the logo (btop's banner family). The signal/renice/msgbox overlays never show it, so their being open stops the animation.
logoTick(): \ClosureThe logo-frame tick Cmd for the current pick. One frame step per fire (ArtLoop's own frameSeconds drives the on-screen cadence through the per-art elapsed clock); the delay is capped at 0.1 s so a slow first frame still lands promptly, mirroring dataTick()'s capture pattern. Precondition: a logo is picked — every call site arms behind logoAnimating()/the applyConfig pick guard, so a null here is a wiring bug and fails loud rather than pacing an invisible dummy frame.
context(string $box): PanelContextThe input context for $box as of NOW: current config, current layout, and the box rectangle (null while hidden or behind the size notice). Built per call, so it is never stale after a toggle, option write or resize.
applyOptions(array $set): arrayValidate and apply option writes in order (btop Config::set: a value its validator rejects is never stored; the rest still apply), then route the result through applyConfig(). A shown_boxes value that would not fit the terminal is refused like a 1-4 toggle (btop's options menu runs the same Term::get_min_size check) and opens the size-error box.
quitCmd(): \ClosureEvery quit: save first when btop's clean_quit would (save_config_on_exit and a pending write), then quit.
stateSave(): ?\ClosureThe proc tree-state write (#1791c, proc_tree_persist_state) still pending at exit, or null. Runs on every quit path next to the config save, and from bin/candy-top after the Program returns (signals, crash); answers \SugarCraft\Top\State\TreeStateSavedMsg.
exitSave(): ?\ClosureThe save btop's clean_quit performs, or null when it would not write: no file, save_config_on_exit off, or nothing changed (btop write_new). bin/candy-top runs it after the Program returns — a SIGTERM / SIGHUP / SIGINT (all trapped by sugar-core's Program::run()) stops the loop without passing quitCmd(), and a quit-time save that failed left the flag set — and reports a failure on STDERR.
saveCmd(): ?\ClosureThe Cmd writing the current config atomically (ConfigFile::write()); answers ConfigSavedMsg. Null without a file.
reloadCmd(): \Closurectrl+r (btop SIGUSR2): read config.conf over the current values and rescan the themes, inside the Cmd.

HostInfo final class

Facts about the host that are fixed for the run and that the frame layout needs before the first sample arrives: the cpu model shown on the cores sub-box, the logical cpu count that sizes it, and the user/host names for the clock's /user /host tokens, and the container engine candy-top runs inside (ContainerEngine, btop Cpu::container_engine; '' on a host), shown on the cpu title in place of the x ctr button, and whether it runs libvirt/KVM guests (vmHost, VmFleet::present()), which shows the VM dashboard's vms title button, and whether it has a BMC device node (bmcHost, bmcPresent()), which shows the ipmi box's IPMI button.

MethodSummary
static new(string $cpuName = '', int $coreCount = 1, string $user = '', string $host = '', bool $hasSensors = false, bool $hasCpuHz = false, string $containerEngine = '', bool $vmHost = false, bool $bmcHost = false): selfExplicit facts (tests, fake runs). Names are sanitized for display.

withBmcHost(bool $bmcHost): selfCopy saying whether this host has a BMC device node — the cpu title then offers the ipmi box's IPMI button (--fake sets it for its fake BMC).

Existence only: a node this user cannot open still shows the button, and the box then says why (\SugarCraft\Top\Collect\Ipmi\IpmiState::NoAccess).
static detect(?Paths $paths = null): selfRead the live host (or a fixture tree via $paths). Never throws.
static hasSensors(Paths $paths): boolbtop get_sensors' got_sensors: at least one temperature sensor was found — an hwmon chip with a temp*_input (directly or under device/), the coretemp platform hwmon, or a thermal zone with a temp file. An empty or fan-only /sys/class/hwmon is NOT a sensor. The discovery is Temp's own port of get_sensors, so the layout's temp columns and the cpu box's readings can never disagree.
static trimName(string $name): stringbtop trim_name: reduce a /proc/cpuinfo "model name" to its model — Xeon / Core 2 Duo / Intel names keep the token after "CPU", Ryzen keeps "Ryzen" plus two tokens, anything else drops the vendor boilerplate and everything from "@" on.

SelfUpdate final class

candy-top self-update — replace the running phar with the latest published one, verified before the swap, with the pre-swap copy kept for a one-shot rollback.

MethodSummary
static useErrorStreamForTesting(mixed $stream): voidRoutes this verb's stderr lines to $stream (pass null to hand the stream back). The suite reads the refusal/mismatch wording this way without spawning a child process.
static run(array $options = [], ?ClientInterface $http = null, ?string $releasesUrl = null, ?string $pharPath = null, ?string $currentVersion = null, ?string $publicKey = null, ?string $osFamily = null): int
static selectRelease(array $releases): ?arrayThe newest candy-top release in a decoded GitHub release list that carries both required assets, or null when none does.
static selectLatestRelease(array $releases): ?arrayThe latest train's release in a decoded GitHub release list, or null when it carries none with both required assets.
static parseSidecar(string $body): ?stringThe lowercase 64-hex-digit digest a sidecar signs with, or null when it is not that shape. Fails closed on uppercase hex, on a short digest, and on anything the sha256sum spelling does not produce.
static sidecarName(string $body): stringThe file name a sidecar declares after its digest ('' when it names nothing). The digest alone would verify bytes of UNKNOWN provenance; the name is what ties it to the phar asset specifically.
static verifyDetached(string $payload, string $signatureBody, string $publicKeyBase64): boolPure Ed25519 detached verification: is $signatureBody the base64 of a signature by $publicKeyBase64 over exactly $payload? Every malformed shape — empty payload, non-strict base64, wrong-length raw halves, a missing sodium extension — answers FALSE (refuse), never an exception and never a trust. Surrounding whitespace is tolerated in both base64 slots because release-asset bodies carry trailing newlines.
static composerRefusal(): stringThe loud composer-mode refusal, verbatim: what to run instead, stated as the exact command. Public and pure so the refusal text is pinned without needing a non-phar "phar" to point the swap machinery at.

AcceleratorKind enum

What an accelerator device is: a GPU, or an NPU (btop #985 Intel NPU, #1839 AMD NPU). Both PRs append the NPU to btop's gpus[] and flip the box labels (is_npu_device / box_label); here the kind travels on the device and GpuSnapshot keeps NPUs in their own list so GPU averages and totals never include them (#985 review).

Cases: Gpu · Npu

PHP also provides cases(), from() and tryFrom().

MethodSummary
label(): stringThe box/row label btop prints: "GPU" or "NPU".
memoryLabel(): stringThe memory label: btop shows "VRAM" for a GPU, #985 "RAM" for an NPU.

AsyncSampling interface

A collector whose sample() forks base-system children and can do the same work without blocking the loop (S-P02): FreeBsd\ReplayProbe answers the collector's reads from loop-delivered child output instead of fork-and-wait. The Source layer asks asyncSampling() before choosing the promise path, so a collector over a fixture or a plain live probe keeps its blocking sample() byte for byte.

MethodSummary
asyncSampling(): boolTrue only when sampleAsync() really avoids blocking children.
sampleAsync(): PromiseInterfaceWhat sample() returns, delivered on the loop; never rejects.

What the ctr box samples after a process scan — btop PR #1873 Ctr::collect(procs): group the processes by container, then read each container's own figures. Live: Containers (cgroup v2 + the docker socket); --fake: \SugarCraft\Top\Source\Fake\FakeContainers.

heldFrom(?self $prev): self#1008 for one device: every column that is unmeasured now but was measured in $prev keeps the previous value, so a row never loses a column on one N/A reading. A different device (index or bus id changed) is not merged. This is the merge CpuPanel::holdDevice() performs, carrying the identity fields too.
memPercent(): floatMemory used as a percent of total; UNMEASURED when either is unknown.

GpuOutcome enum

How one nvidia-smi query ended — the distinction Gpu's memoization hinges on: Absent is permanent (no binary, driver refuses, non-zero exit), Timeout is transient (a GPU busy resetting or a slow driver call) and must be retried, never memoized.

Cases: Ok · Absent · Timeout

PHP also provides cases().

MethodSummary
static unescape(string $text): stringsystemd unit-name unescaping (systemd-escape --unescape): every \xNN becomes byte 0xNN; anything else is kept verbatim.
static scope(string $cgroup): ?arrayThe outermost libvirt/machined VM segment of a cgroup path.
static isQemuBinary(string $argv0): boolargv[0] names a QEMU system emulator: qemu-system-*, kvm or qemu-kvm (basename).
static fromCmdline(?string $cmdline): ?VmInfoThe VM facts in a raw (NUL-separated) /proc/[pid]/cmdline; null when it is not a QEMU command line (see the class doc).
static smp(string $value): intBoot vCPUs from a -smp value: the implied / cpus= count ("2,sockets=2" → 2, "cpus=4" → 4); when that is absent or 0, QEMU derives it from the topology, so sockets × dies × clusters × cores × threads; nothing usable → UNMEASURED_INT.
static memory(string $value): intGuest RAM bytes from a -m value (QEMU qemu_strtosz_MiB): the implied / size= amount, a decimal number with an optional B/K/M/G/T/P/E suffix (either case), MiB when there is none — "size=6291456k", "2048", "4G", "1.5G,slots=2,maxmem=8G". Malformed, zero or overflowing → UNMEASURED_INT.
static machineName(string $name): stringlibvirt's machine-name sanitising of a domain name (virDomainMachineNameAppendValid): hostname characters only, runs of '.'/'-' collapse to their first, a leading or trailing '.'/'-' is dropped. Used to cross-check a scope name against guest=.
static fromCgroupPath(string $cgroup, ?string $cmdline = null): ?ContainerRefThe ContainerRef for a VM recognised from one cgroup path (null when the path has no VM segment) — cmdline facts merged in when given.
static fromBareCmdline(?string $cmdline): ?ContainerRefNon-libvirt qemu: a qemu binary (basename rule) with a -name. cgroupPath is '' — the process owns no VM cgroup.
static vcpuThreads(Paths $paths, int $pid): arrayvCPU threads of a VM process: /proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/comm CPU <n>/KVM (QEMU -name …,debug-threads=on, which libvirt always sets; /TCG, /HVF… accepted too), else a task cgroup ending in vcpu<n> below a VM scope (libvirt without debug-threads). One directory listing plus one or two small reads per thread — call it on demand (a detail view), not every tick for every pid.

DrmScan final class

One DRM fdinfo scan's result (DrmFdinfo).

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly array $clients, public readonly bool $measured, public readonly bool $ran = true, public readonly bool $complete = true, public readonly bool $partial = false)
static none(): selfNo scan this cycle: nothing asked for one.
utilization(string $pdev): floatBusy percent of the device at PCI slot $pdev: - UNMEASURED before the second scan, or when every client on it was first seen this scan; - UNMEASURED before the first discovery pass completes (clients not yet reached would read as idle); - with no visible client after a completed pass: 0.0 — exact when every fd dir was readable, a LOWER BOUND when partial (a non-root monitor cannot read other users' fd dirs; fdinfo only shows what this uid may ptrace). Not UNMEASURED: a sentinel here would let a consumer's #1008 hold freeze the last busy value forever once the visible client exits; - with visible clients: their busiest engine class — again a lower bound when partial. lowerBound() says which; backends copy it onto GpuDevice::$utilizationLowerBound. A client opened since its pid was last walked is invisible until the next discovery pass reaches it (DrmFdinfo).
lowerBound(): boolUtilizations from this scan are floors: some fd dirs were unreadable.
processes(array $index): arrayPer-process rows, one per (pid, device), for the devices in $index.

IntelNpu final class

Mirrors aristocratos/btop #985's intel_vpu NPU detection (and its successor fork PR #1789's frequency read; src/linux/btop_collect.cpp): Intel NPUs through the intel_vpu (ivpu) driver's sysfs. Pure sysfs: - utilization = Δnpu_busy_time_us / Δwall µs × 100 (a cumulative counter, so the first sample is UNMEASURED); - memory = npu_memory_utilization (bytes in use; no total exists); - clock = npu_current_frequency_mhz, max npu_max_frequency_mhz. Devices are found under /sys/class/accel and /sys/bus/pci/drivers/intel_vpu (#985 reads the latter). Names from pci.ids, else "Intel NPU". Reported with kind NPU, so they land in GpuSnapshot::$npus and never in a GPU average.

Settled final class

No upstream counterpart (btop collects synchronously inside Gpu::collect): this is PHP-only plumbing for the promise-shaped runners. Reads a react/promise that may already be settled. The GPU collectors are written once, as promise chains: with a blocking runner every link settles synchronously (react/promise runs then() callbacks of a settled promise at once), so value() unwraps the result on the spot; with the loop runner the same chain resolves later.

MethodSummary
static peek(PromiseInterface $promise): array[true, value] when $promise has fulfilled; [false, null] while it is pending. A rejection is rethrown.
static value(PromiseInterface $promise): mixedThe fulfilled value.

SmiProcess final class

Mirrors aristocratos/btop Gpu::Nvml's bounded nvidia-smi child (the process-list fallback, src/linux/btop_collect.cpp) — as the GPU collectors' view of AsyncCommand, which owns the spawn, the timeout, the reaping, the registry and the shutdown hook (shared with every other helper child, ipmitool included). This adapter only maps a CommandResult onto the GPU memoisation vocabulary: Ok keeps stdout, any other exit or no spawn is Absent (permanent), an overrun is Timeout (retried).

MethodSummary
static run(array $argv, float $timeout = self::TIMEOUT): arrayBlocking: [Ok, stdout] on exit 0, [Absent, ''] on any other exit or when nothing could be spawned, [Timeout, ''] past $timeout.
static launch(array $argv, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, float $timeout = self::TIMEOUT): PromiseInterfaceNon-blocking: the same outcomes as run(), delivered by the loop. Resolves on the loop thread; never rejects.
static liveCount(): intChildren spawned and not yet closed (every helper child, not only nvidia-smi).
static shutdown(float $wait = self::REAP_WAIT): voidSIGKILL and reap every live helper child, waiting at most $wait seconds.

IpmiParser final class

Text parsers for the ipmitool commands the ipmi box runs. Written against real captures from two very different BMCs (ASUS/AMI and HP iLO 4) and forgiving by design: an unknown line is skipped, never fatal, because every vendor adds its own rows, units and spacing.

MethodSummary
static sensorList(string $text): arrayipmitool sensor list → one IpmiSensor per row, in BMC order. Rows with fewer than four columns (warnings, blank lines) are skipped.
static sdrElist(string $text): arrayipmitool sdr elist → one IpmiSensor per row: name | id | status | entity | reading, where the reading is "45 degrees C", "19.60 percent, Transition to Running", a discrete state ("Fully Redundant", "Device Absent"), "Disabled", "No Reading" or empty. No thresholds — merge() adds those from one sensor list. Against a local SDR cache (-S) this walk takes ~0.5 s where sensor list takes 4-29 s (measured on HP iLO 4 and ASUS/AMI).
static merge(array $values, array $thresholds): arrayValues from $values (sdr elist) with the thresholds of the same name from $thresholds (sensor list), in $values' order.
static dcmi(string $text): ?IpmiPoweripmitool dcmi power reading → the reading, or null when the BMC gave none.
static chassis(string $text): ?IpmiChassisipmitool chassis status → its flags, or null when there was no "System Power" line.
static selInfo(string $text): ?IpmiSelipmitool sel info → the fill level, or null without an "Entries" line.
static selLatest(string $text): stringThe newest line of ipmitool sel elist last 1 (or sel list): id | date | time | sensor | event | direction → "date time · sensor · event · direction" with the record id dropped.
static info(string $mc, string $fru, string $lan = '', ?int $channel = null): IpmiInfomc info + fru print 0 + lan print <channel> → the header facts. Any of the three may be '' (that command failed).
static lanAddress(string $lan): stringThe address lan print answered with; '' when none or unconfigured (0.0.0.0).
static vendor(?int $id, string $name): stringThe BMC maker's short name: a known IANA number, else the first word of "Manufacturer Name".
static pairs(string $text): array"Key : value" lines → map, first occurrence wins; continuation lines ( : User : MD5, bare list items) are skipped.

A sensor list sorted into what the box draws: temperatures, fans, voltages, power supplies, other power rails, currents and the fan redundancy state. IpmiSnapshot final class

One round of the ipmi collector. Rounds are partial on purpose — the cheap power reading comes every round, the multi-second SDR walk (sensor list), chassis status and SEL only on the slow cadence, the static header once — so every part is nullable and null means "not read this round, keep what you had" (the panel merges, #1008-style), never "gone".

MethodSummary

SdrCache final class

The private home of the ipmi reader's SDR cache (ipmitool sdr dump).

MethodSummary
setLivenessOracle(\Closure $liveness): voidOverride the liveness oracle (tests; the seam that lets a suite exercise a /proc-less, posix-less host on a machine that has both).
static open(?string $base = null): ?selfThe private directory under $base (default: $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR when it is an absolute writable dir, else the system temp dir), created 0700 if missing; null when it cannot be made private.
sweep(): intRemove the caches left by candy-tops that are gone (killed before their exit hook ran). Files of live pids — another candy-top of the same user — are kept. Returns how many were removed. Where the host carries no liveness oracle at all (no ext-posix and no /proc: the FreeBSD-without-procfs and macOS legs this collector targets as an option), files of unverifiable pids are NEVER guessed away — deleting one from under a live long-running candy-top would yank the cache it re-reads via -S <cache> all session — and are reported through self::indeterminate() instead of silently accumulating.
indeterminate(): arrayCache files the last self::sweep() found but could not attribute to a live or dead process because the host has no liveness oracle; empty on every host where the verdict is decidable.
reserve(): ?stringReserve a fresh 0600 file for one dump and register its removal; null when it cannot be created exclusively.
release(string $file): voidRemove one reserved file (a failed dump, or the reader going away).
releaseAll(): voidRemove every reserved file — the exit hook.

AbsoluteSearchPath final class

The PATH sweep both binary finders share: existing absolute directories only, realpath'd, in PATH order, de-duplicated.

MethodSummary
static directories(?string $path = null, ?string $osFamily = null): array

AsyncCommand final class

One bounded helper child (nvidia-smi, ipmitool, ...) — the only place candy-top's collectors spawn a long-lived process. Two ways to drive it, sharing the spawn, the timeout and the reaping: - run() blocks until the child exits or the timeout passes (startup probes, scripted tests, any caller outside the loop); - launch() returns at once and collects stdout through a loop read stream, so a slow tool (nvidia-smi pmon 0.25-1 s, an ipmitool sensor list SDR walk 1.7-4 s) never stalls input or rendering.

MethodSummary
static run(array $argv, float $timeout = self::TIMEOUT, int $maxBytes = self::MAX_OUTPUT): CommandResultBlocking: the child's CommandResult — Ok on exit 0, Failed on any other exit, Absent when nothing could be spawned, Timeout past $timeout.
static launch(array $argv, ?LoopInterface $loop = null, float $timeout = self::TIMEOUT, int $maxBytes = self::MAX_OUTPUT, array $env = []): PromiseInterfaceNon-blocking: the same outcomes as run(), delivered by the loop. Resolves on the loop thread; never rejects.
static liveCount(): intChildren spawned and not yet closed (running, or killed and awaiting their reap).
static shutdown(float $wait = self::REAP_WAIT): voidSIGKILL every live child and reap it, waiting at most $wait seconds in all — the exit hook (also callable by tests).
static liveFor(string $program): intLive children (running, or killed and not yet reaped) of program $program (argv[0]) — a caller can refuse to stack another child on one stuck in uninterruptible sleep.
static withSpawnFactory(?callable $factory): voidTest seam (like the sibling subsystems' runner closures): replace the OS spawn behind run() and launch(). The factory takes the gate-checked argv and the allowlisted child environment and returns the [process, pipes] shape of proc_open for a child it spawned itself — or null for a spawn failure (the Absent path). The registry, the kill ladder and the reaping all run over the injected child exactly as over a real one, which is what makes the timing around the loop statable: launch a child, decline to run the loop, and the exited-but-unclosed residue candy-top-042 is about is on the table as a fact (a real kernel stages no SIGKILL-immune child — a group-stopped one still dies, which the wedged-driver shape cannot be faked, only accounted). Null (default) keeps the real proc_open; a malformed return is a programming error and throws.

CommandOutcome enum

How one bounded child ended (AsyncCommand): - Ok: exited 0; - Failed: exited with another code (or was killed by a signal it did not get from us) — the program ran and said no; - Absent: nothing could be spawned (no such executable, proc_open disabled); - Timeout: still running at the deadline, SIGKILLed; - TooLarge: wrote more than its output cap, SIGKILLed (a runaway child must not grow candy-top's memory without bound).

Cases: Ok · Failed · Absent · Timeout · TooLarge

PHP also provides cases().

CommandResult final class

What one AsyncCommand child produced: its outcome, exit code (null unless it exited on its own) and everything it wrote to stdout. stdout is kept on a non-zero exit too — ipmitool, for one, prints the rows it could read before failing on the next.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly CommandOutcome $outcome, public readonly string $stdout = '', public readonly ?int $exit = null, public readonly float $seconds = 0.0)
static absent(): self
ok(): bool

MethodSummary

has(string $key): boolWhether $key is a known option.

int(string $key): intInteger option value — btop Config::getI.

withParsed(string $key, string $raw, bool $fromFile = false): selfCopy with $key set from its config-file spelling (True, 2000, an unquoted string) — what the options menu's text field produces. $fromFile selects the loader's law (shown_boxes unvalidated, as btop).
withShownBoxesSettled(?int $gpuCount): selfCopy with shown_boxes settled against the machine — btop.cpp's post-load set_boxes check: the file loader accepts shown_boxes verbatim, so an unknown box name, a gpuN beyond the $gpuCount GPUs actually detected, or more than GpuPanels::MAX gpu boxes (btop PR #1730) resets the list to "cpu mem net proc". A null $gpuCount skips only the index check (the GPUs have not been sampled). An empty list is legitimate (btop then draws no boxes) and is kept.
shownBoxesSettlement(?int $gpuCount): ?stringWhy withShownBoxesSettled() would reset this list, or null when it stands. The settlement used to be silent: the box layout a user hand- picked could vanish on a startup where a GPU went undetected, and the reset was then what the next save wrote back. Callers that own a notice channel (bin, the reload report) surface this instead.
withPersistedFrom(Config $other): selfCopy with every PERSISTED option taken from $other, runtime state (tty_mode, proc_filter, show_detailed, ...) kept — what a config reload does (btop init_config re-runs Config::load over the live maps, which only ever touches descriptions keys). $other's values were validated when it was built, so no law re-runs here.
withSessionOverrides(array $changes): selfApply $changes as session-only launch overrides — btop's -p/-t/-u (S-O06): the running session sees the new values, but every write of the config file keeps the pre-override value until a session-side set of the same key claims it, and a ctrl+r reload takes the file wholesale.
persistedValue(string $key): bool|int|stringThe value the config file carries for $name: a session-only launch override never writes, so ConfigWriter renders the pre-override value while the live session still runs on value() (S-O06).
persistedDiffers(Config $other): boolWhether any persisted option differs from $other — btop's write_new trigger (any Config::set of a descriptions key).
asString(string $key): string$key's value in btop's menu spelling — Config::getAsString: bools True/False, ints as digits, strings as stored.
flipped(string $key): selfCopy with the bool option $key inverted — btop Config::flip.
withUpdateMs(int $ms): selfCopy with update_ms clamped into [100, 86_400_000].
withSessionUpdateMs(int $ms): selfCopy with update_ms applied as a session-only launch override — btop's -u: the frame period changes for this run, the config file keeps what it had until a session-side set claims the key (S-O06).
withPreset(Preset $preset): selfCopy with $preset applied — btop Config::apply_preset minus the terminal-size gate (the app checks the minimum size before calling). P=1 sets cpu_bottom / mem_below_net / proc_left for those boxes; each box's graph symbol lands on graph_symbol_<box> (gpuN share graph_symbol_gpu); the box list becomes shown_boxes (gpu slots back to the default order, btop set_boxes). A proc box also sets proc_box_width_percent (btop PR #1476): its W field clamped to 0-100, or the 55 default when W is absent or default — so applying a preset always resets a width the user nudged with Shift+arrows.
withSessionPreset(Preset $preset): selfCopy with $preset applied as a session-only launch override — btop's -p: layout and symbols change for this run, the config file keeps what it had until a session-side set claims a key (S-O06).
updateMs(): intData/frame period in milliseconds (default 2000).
colorTheme(): stringTheme name: "Default", "TTY" or a .theme file stem.
graphSymbol(): stringGlobal graph symbol family: braille | block | block2 | tty.
graphSymbolFor(string $box): stringEffective graph symbol for $box: its graph_symbol_<box> override, or graph_symbol when that says "default"; gpuN read graph_symbol_gpu. TTY mode forces "tty" for every box (btop_draw.cpp cpu box: tty_mode ? "tty" : graph_symbol_cpu).
shownBoxes(): array
presets(): PresetsThe parsed presets option, built-in preset 0 first.
procSorting(): stringproc_sorting: one of Schema::PROC_SORTING.
withProcBoxWidthPercent(int $percent): selfCopy with proc_box_width_percent clamped into [0, 100] — the Shift/Alt+Shift+arrow key path of btop PR #1476, which pins at the bounds instead of erroring. The layout further clamps to the min/max box widths the window allows without touching the stored value.
procBoxWidthPercent(): intproc_box_width_percent (btop PR #1476): proc box width % when mem or net is shown, 0-100.
showCoreFreq(): stringshow_core_freq (btop PR #1785): off | value | graph — per-core frequency in the cpu box.
memSelected(): stringmem_selected (btop PR #1747): "default" for the stacked mem meters, or the one metric (used | available | cached | free | swap_used) drawn as a single full-height graph.
disksOrder(): arraydisks_order (btop PR #1700) as a list: mountpoints (and the swap pseudo-disk) to show first, in order. Whitespace-split like btop's ssplit, duplicates dropped keeping the first — btop's apply_disks_order skips a mountpoint already placed.
tempScale(): stringtemp_scale: celsius | fahrenheit | kelvin | rankine.
clockFormat(): stringstrftime clock format with btop's /host /user /uptime tokens; "" disables the clock.

HelpMenu final class

btop's help menu: the banner over a help box listing every key from KeyTable, grouped into the named KeyTable::SECTIONS, each section drawn as its own framed box, and the boxes flowed through two columns, paged when the terminal cannot hold the whole grid.

MethodSummary
static new(): self
capturesInput(): bool
minSize(): arraybtop Menu::process: main, options, help and the signal chooser need 80x24.
static widthFor(int $cols): intBox width for a terminal: btop's 78 at the 80-column minimum, up to 166, never wider than two cells under the terminal (the 78-in-80 margins stay symmetric).
static columnsFor(int $width): intGrid columns a box of this width fits — always two: the third column the adaptive grid once earned (110+ cells) was too narrow to hold a framed section box and its descriptions. Kept as a method because the width math and the tests flow through it.
static columnWidth(int $width, int $columns): intCells of one grid column inside a box of this width.
static geometry(int $cols, int $rows, int $delta = 0): arrayThe help geometry, 1-based: [x, y, height, pages].
static logoDelta(OverlayContext $c): intRows the resolved logo adds over the banner; 0 keeps every geometry and paint term at its legacy value (byte-identical fallback). Two gates: the box needs at least a 6-row interior (border, title, separator, one key row, footer, border) before a logo is worth the squeeze, AND the true delta'd extents — with y centred/clamped by geometry() the bottom border can ride past the last row while the interior floor still passes (rows-6-δ beats 6 at heights where the content or clamp term wins). Delegates the height/pages math to geometry() itself so the two can never diverge.
update(Msg $msg, OverlayContext $context): OverlayResult
paint(Surface $surface, OverlayContext $c): void
static forgetPlanCache(): voidDrop every memoised plan — the seam for translation-table swaps.
static plan(int $width, int $perColumn): arrayThe whole grid as pages of framed section boxes, independent of the terminal beyond width and per-column height: every section becomes a box (heading + its rows in roster order, descriptions wrapped to the box interior minus the key column), over-tall sections are first cut into sized segments, and the ordered boxes are then placed by a greedy pass — each box takes the FITTING column with the LEAST used height (ties to the left column), a column takes a box when used + spacer + height stays within $perColumn (the spacer is one blank row, needed only when the column already stacks a box), and the page turns only when NEITHER column fits. Later, smaller boxes therefore fill the shorter column's hole instead of trailing the first one down, and for every non-last page the first box of the next page provably fits NEITHER column of it — only that first box: a later, smaller one on the same page might still have squeezed into a residual hole, and the pass lets the turn stand rather than reach past the box in front of it, so the invariant is reading-order-stable maximality, not order-free optimality. Boxes are never reordered against reading order; a page reads column-major (left stack, then right), and a split section's continuation rides whichever column has room, so its second frame can sit left of its first — the embedded headings keep that legible either way. A box is atomic; a section taller than one whole column splits into balanced segments, EACH a framed box re-embedding the heading, so every row stays visible. Pure and deterministic — the goldens and self::geometry() byte-pin this layout.
static usedRows(array $columns): intThe content rows one planned page actually consumes: the deepest box bottom across the two columns — each box rides at its column offset row and is count(lines) + 2 rows tall (its own two borders), the one-row spacer between stacked boxes is already inside row, and a trailing spacer never exists. usedRows + self::CHROME_ROWS is the page's fitted outer-box height in self::paint(). Precondition for the fitted box to hide nothing: a page planned at capacity height - self::CHROME_ROWS has usedRows <= height - self::CHROME_ROWS whenever that capacity is at least 3 (below it the greedy overflows the head of a column exactly as the old atomic flow did, and paint's min() then keeps the legacy global box height). Pure — a function of self::plan()'s output, deterministic like the planner itself.

GpuHold final class

btop #1008 for accelerators, bounded: a device that answers N/A keeps its last measured columns (GpuDevice::heldFrom()), but only for limit() consecutive samples in which it measured NOTHING (a GpuDevice::unmeasured() stand-in — its backend failed or it was unplugged) or in which the whole snapshot came back without GPUs. Past that the device shows its stand-in (every column n/a) and the caller drops its graph history (apply() returns the expired indexes), so a GPU that is gone for good stops showing frozen numbers. A device that still answers some column is held column by column without limit (one N/A reading never drops a column), as before.

MethodSummary
static new(): self
static limit(int $updateMs): intConsecutive silent samples a device is held for at $updateMs: max(5, ceil(30 s / update_ms)).

GpuSampling final class

Collect-time retuning of a GPU source for what its consumers need — the shared feed (GpuFeed) tunes it for the union of every consumer's GpuDemand, the startup probe for the config alone: - shown_gpus → Accelerators::withVendors() (btop's vendor filter; NPUs are never filtered); - per-process collection (#1552) → Accelerators::withProcesses() only while processesWanted() — the hook the proc box's GPU columns decide. It flips the collector only on a CHANGE: re-calling withProcesses(true) would clear a nvidia-smi pmon "unsupported" mark every tick. \SugarCraft\Top\Source\Fake\FakeGpu takes the per-process switch too; any other source (a scripted test source) is returned unchanged.

Three detail levels by the box's interior, the way the gpu box's #1881 levels degrade: - FULL (≥ 64×14, or a band ≥ 100×5): titled sub-panels — power (braille gauge, BMC window, per-PSU in/out bars with efficiency, power rails), status (fault chips, SEL fill and newest entry), temperatures (gradient meters to each sensor's own critical limit), fans (bars to the threshold or the fastest fan seen, redundancy badge) and voltages (centred deviation bars between the thresholds) — in 2, 3 or 4 columns by width; - COMPACT (≥ 34×6): the gauge beside the hottest temperatures, a fan summary and the fault chips; - TINY: one line each for power, the hottest temperatures and faults.

MethodSummary
static paint(Region $r, PanelFrame $frame, IpmiData $d): void
static pickTemps(array $temps, int $slots): arrayTemperatures in $rows slots: intake first, then BMC order when all fit, else hottest relative to its limit first.

PowerGauge final class

A semicircular "radio" gauge drawn in braille (2×4 dots per cell, so the arc is smooth at any size): a thick outer arc filled from the left to the reading, coloured by position along a theme gradient, the rest a thin meter_bg rail; a thin inner arc spanning the BMC window's min..max with the average marked; and a needle at the reading.

MethodSummary
static height(int $width): intRows that fit a gauge $width cells wide: its dot radius is min(width, 4·height) / 1 — a round arc needs height ≈ width / 4.
static render(Ink $ink, int $width, int $height, float $value, ?float $min, ?float $avg, ?float $max, string $gradient = 'cpu'): array$height SGR rows of exactly $width cells.

PowerHistory final class

The draw over time under the power gauge: a braille area chart, two samples per cell (newest at the right edge), filled up to each sample, each row coloured by its height along a theme gradient (the top rows are the hot end), with a dotted meter_bg baseline where no sample is yet.

MethodSummary
static spark(Ink $ink, int $width, array $values, float $low, float $high, string $gradient): stringA one-row braille sparkline, two samples per cell, newest at the right; each cell coloured along $gradient by its higher sample's place between $low and $high.

SugarCraft\Top\State

TreeState final class

The remembered proc-tree collapse choices (btop #1791c proc_tree_persist_state): process-name ancestry path => collapsed.

MethodSummary
static empty(): self
static key(array $names): ?stringThe key for a root-first name path, or null when it cannot be stored (empty, too deep, an empty or over-long name, or a name holding the separator).
static fromArray(array $data, int $now): selfDecode a state file's payload, dropping whatever does not validate: a wrong version yields the empty state, a malformed entry is skipped, a stale one (older than MAX_AGE at $now) is dropped, and only the newest MAX_ENTRIES survive.
toArray(int $now): arrayThe payload to store, oldest first; untouched-this-session entries keep their time, touched ones are stamped $now. A path that is not valid UTF-8 cannot round-trip through JSON and is left out.
withinBytes(int $maxBytes, int $now): arrayA copy that encodes within $maxBytes under toArray() at $now: the file budget is spent by dropping from the oldest end of the oldest-first store — the least recently used choices go first, the same order capped() enforces. Fits is monotone in the number of kept entries, so a binary search over the keep-newest-k count pins the largest safe k in log2(n) encodes instead of a full re-encode per drop.
lookup(string $key): ?boolThe remembered choice for $key, or null when there is none.
remember(string $key, bool $collapsed): selfRemember $collapsed for $key as the most recent choice.
touched(array $keys): selfMark $keys (paths that matched a running process) as used now, so a choice still in use never ages out. The same instance when nothing changed.
count(): int
keys(): array

TreeStateFile final class

Where the proc-tree collapse choices live between runs: $XDG_STATE_HOME/candy-top/tree-state.json, else $HOME/.local/state/candy-top/tree-state.json.

MethodSummary
static new(string $path): self
static defaultPath(?array $env = null): ?stringThe XDG state path, or null when neither XDG_STATE_HOME nor HOME is usable. A relative XDG_STATE_HOME is invalid per the base-directory spec and ignored.
path(): string
load(int $now): TreeStateThe stored state as of $now; empty on any problem with the file.
write(TreeState $state, int $now): intAtomically store $state, stamping entries touched this session with $now. A payload too large for the read-side MAX_BYTES gate is never left to land and be silently discarded by the next start: the least recently used head is pruned first (the binary-search leg of TreeState::withinBytes()), and the number of dropped entries is returned so the caller can report the reason.

Result of a tree-state write: which change revision reached disk, or why it did not. A failure is not shown in-session (the state is a convenience); bin/candy-top reports a failed exit-time save on STDERR. $note carries a save that succeeded with a cause worth naming — entries pruned to keep the file under the read-side budget — and is reported the same way.

Logo final class

The animated/logo alternative to the block-letter Banner: ANSI art from sugar-animation, re-picked every time a menu opens (the App calls pick() again on each transition into the main, options or help menu) and painted in place of the banner.

MethodSummary
static pick(ColorProfile $profile): ?AnsiArtThe logo for $profile's depth tag, or null when the caller must paint the legacy banner (switched off, corpus missing, nothing resolvable).
static paint(Surface $surface, int $y, AnsiArt $art, int $frameIndex, Ink $ink): voidBlit frame $frameIndex of $art centred with its top row at 0-based $y, the same geometry Banner::paint uses (centre minus the one-cell btop offset). Cells past the right edge are skipped by the surface's own clip; a row taller than the surface simply never lands.
static blockFits(int $topRow, int $bottomLine, int $rows): boolFit gate shared by the three banner-family menus' logoDelta(): a delta-shifted block spans the logo's top row at 0-based $topRow through the box's bottom border at 1-based $bottomLine, and every row of it must land on-screen. The clamped/centred anchors plus the content-driven height terms mean a simple interior-floor check can pass while the bottom border rides past the last row — the true extents are cheap to compute at the call site, so compute them and ask here. Failing the gate means falling back to delta 0 (the legacy banner): a clipped border is worse than no logo.
static resetForTesting(): voidDrop the memoised library and picks (test seams around env changes).
static picksForTesting(): intRandom draws attempted since the last resetForTesting() — lets tests pin that every menu open really advanced the draw (explicit slugs never count: they are memo lookups, not rolls).

Region final class

A rectangle of a Surface with its own origin: (0, 0) is the rectangle's top-left cell and every write is clipped to it. This is what a \SugarCraft\Top\Panel\Panel paints into — it can reach its own border rows (btop embeds buttons and readouts there) but can never spill into a neighbouring box, whatever width its content computes.

Surface final class

The per-frame cell grid every box, panel and embed paints into.

MethodSummary
static new(int $width, int $height, string $base = ''): self
bounds(): Rect
region(Rect $rect): RegionA clipped view onto $rect with rect-local coordinates.
put(int $x, int $y, string $text, string $sgr = '', ?Rect $clip = null): intWrite plain $text at ($x, $y) in style $sgr, clipped to $clip (default: the whole surface). Control characters are dropped — a process name or hostname must never smuggle an escape into the frame.
ansi(int $x, int $y, string $line, ?Rect $clip = null, string $sgr = ''): intWrite a line that carries its own SGR escapes (e.g. a pre-rendered graph row or a bold title run). Each SGR escape updates the folded state (a later fg REPLACES the earlier one, 22 drops bold, 0 resets); every other escape sequence is discarded. $sgr is the starting style.
fill(Rect $rect, string $sgr = ''): voidPaint $rect with spaces in style $sgr.
dim(string $sgr): voidRe-style every cell as $sgr, keeping the glyphs — btop's overlay backdrop (btop.cpp Runner: Fx::ub + Theme::c("inactive_fg") + Fx::uncolor(output)): every colour and attribute of the frame is stripped and the whole frame is redrawn in one dim colour under the menu.
restyle(int $x, int $y, string $sgr): voidReplace the style of the cell at ($x, $y), keeping its glyph — a post-pass recolour (e.g. BorderFlow). Out of bounds is a no-op.
restyleBoxDrawing(Rect $rect, array $styles, array &$memo, \Closure $resolve): voidRestyle, inside $rect, every box-drawing cell (U+2500..U+257F) whose style is a key of $styles — the BorderFlow hot loop, kept here so it reads the cell array directly (it runs every frame).
glyph(int $x, int $y): stringGlyph at ($x, $y): '' for the right half of a wide cluster.
style(int $x, int $y): stringStyle run at ($x, $y).
lines(): arrayRendered rows: exactly $height of them, each exactly $width cells, each self-contained (starts from a reset, ends with one) so the line-diff renderer can repaint any row alone.
render(): stringThe whole frame, rows joined by "\n".
plainLines(): arrayRows as plain text (no escapes) — the cell-grid view tests assert on.
static canonical(string $sgr): string$sgr (any run of SGR escapes) folded into one canonical escape: attributes ascending, then fg, bg, underline colour; '' when the run leaves nothing set. Non-SGR bytes are ignored.

Untrusted final class

The shared sink for untrusted identifier text: process names, commands and users, container and guest names, engines. Panels scrub invalid UTF-8, replace control bytes with spaces, and — since candy-top-096 — render the invisible bidi and zero-width format characters visibly through sugar-core's display policy, so a locally named process, PTY, container or VM cannot silently reverse or blank a column ("Trojan Source" spoofing against the repo's own documented tool).

MethodSummary
static text(string $s): stringScrub, space-fold the control bytes, then mark the invisible formatters.
